newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR QUOTED MIXED AT TUESDAY'S CLOSE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR QUOTED MIXED AT TUESDAY'S CLOSE.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar was quoted mixed against hard currencies at the close of Tuesday's interbank market which started off quietly but saw increased activity later in the day.
"Contrary to earler expectations (of an eventless market) we observed some swings in the market today," one dealer commented.
He said the local unit appreciated as far as 11.2800/2900 against the key U.S. dollar from 11.2850/2950 at opening, on the back of a "sizeable" amount of inflows from the tobacco sales.
The central Reserve Bank however intervened in the market to mop up the excesses, resulting in the local unit easing to 11.2950/3050, where it closed. This compared with 11.2975/3075 on Monday.

Market analysts say with annual inflation jumping to 22.4 percent in April from 19.9 percent in March, the central bank is likely to keep a tight reign on the local dollar to stop it from appreciating unduly and losing its competitiveness against international currencies.

Against sterling, the Zimbabwe dollar finished Tuesday's session at 18.5600/5800 from 18.5095/5390 but was firmer on the mark at 6.6400/6600 compared to 6.6815/6830 on Monday. It was at 2.5300/5400 versus the rand, weakening slightly from 2.5290/5305.
